issue_context.title: Missing [un]supported APIs annotations in System.Net.NetworkInformation
issue_context.body:
System.Net.NetworkInformation assembly on platforms where it's supported has over 80 PNSE methods but no [un]supported APIs annotation. This degrades user experience when working with the APIs as a significant portion of the assembly is not supported cross-platform.

It should be part of #47228

/cc @jeffhandley @buyaa-n

@buyaa-n any thoughts on why your tool didn't find these?

I run the tool only for cross-platform builds, seems for System.Net.NetworkInformation there is no source built for cross-platform (or when ` Condition="'$(TargetsAnyOS)' != 'true'"`) that is why there is nothing detected. From the existing TFMs seems it is supported on `windows; Linux; OSX; iOS; tvOS; FreeBSD; illumos; Solaris;` so we can add those platforms into the assembly level supported list. If you are expecting individual APIs supposed to be annotated then i have not detected them for now, I am updating the tool to detect incompatible PNSEs in targeted builds, almost finished then, need to run it and analyze the results.
@buyaa-n assigning to you as you are working on the tool update. Is there any ETA or work item tracking it on Analyzer side?

>  Is there any ETA or work item tracking it on Analyzer side?

[The issue](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/42967)  for adding the analyzer is closed in API review as adding it in SKD or runtime repo will be very noisy, so the analyzer I am running is only for one-time detection.  But there is  a related [issue ](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/47228) for detecting unsupported APIs and annotating them
@buyaa-n @jeffhandley is it still on your radar for 6.0? (just double checking it was not forgotten as it is in Networking area ...)
@karelz This is still on our radar, but we're not going to be able to look at it again before the Preview 7 snap; we'll have to follow up before RC1.

Somehow when running build from runtime root folder no warnings logged for this project. But i still see plenty of PNSEs with manual search, so run the build from the project src folder and see the warnings. There is 2 public APIs needs `UnsupportedOSPlatform` annotation for specific platforms (top 2 rows), and 71 APIs defined in internal class and doesn't seem to have any reference internally (remaining rows). > Note that using `SupportedOS` doesn't help here either since that would be `UnknownUnix` which has the same problem as the two OSes above.

Not sure why do you think the `<SupportedPlatform>` hook would not work and what is  `UnknownUnix`? Did already you tried adding `<SupportedPlatform Include="illumos"/>` and `<SupportedPlatform Include="solaris "/>` (might need to add them conditional so that it is not added in unnecessary builds)

Another thing you might want to consider is if the API is only supported on certain platforms better to add SupportedOSPlatform attribute(s) instead of UnsupportedOSPlatform attribute(s)

> better to add SupportedOSPlatform attribute(s) instead of UnsupportedOSPlatform attribute(s)

That's what I've meant with "using SupportedOS doesn't help here either", because the file is conditionally compiled for these 3 platforms: UknownUnix, Solaris, illumos:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/0ea8653e1f0ada5c7a15515430c6f16585911af4/src/libraries/System.Net.NetworkInformation/src/System.Net.NetworkInformation.csproj#L184-L188
Neither of those strings works with `SupportedOSPlatform`/`UnsupportedOSPlatform`. So reversing the condition doesn't help here.

> Did already you tried adding <SupportedPlatform Include="illumos"/> and <SupportedPlatform Include="solaris "/> (might need to add them conditional so that it is not added in unnecessary builds)

What is that? Do we have an example of this? I've never heard or seen this.

> Neither of those strings works with SupportedOSPlatform/UnsupportedOSPlatform. So reversing the condition doesn't help here.

I see, with `Note that using SupportedOS doesn't help` i thought you are talking about `<SupportedPlatform Include="illumos"/> and <SupportedPlatform Include="solaris "/>` properties

> What is that? Do we have an example of this? I've never heard or seen this.

It is a used to add unknown platforms to the `MSBuild` SupportedPlatforms list, you can add `<SupportedPlatform Include="illumos"/> and <SupportedPlatform Include="solaris "/>` item group in your project. Probably with a condition `Condition="'$(TargetsUnknownUnix)' == 'true'"`

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <SupportedPlatform Condition="'$(TargetsUnknownUnix)' == 'true'" Include="illumos"/>
  <SupportedPlatform Condition="'$(TargetsUnknownUnix)' == 'true'" Include="solaris "/>
</ItemGroup>
````

There is really now way how somebody can target them right now AFAIK.

We have them as targets for this project:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8e92a6fe4d89934eba274e2a247c800a725d6de9/src/libraries/System.Net.NetworkInformation/src/System.Net.NetworkInformation.csproj#L4

> I assume that's the reason why it's firing the warnings.

Right when there is a target platform in the TFM that build going to be for that platform for the analyzer. Sounds like the case the API is supported on certain platforms and throws on all others, if you cannot use SupportedOSPlatform attributes with the realistic platforms then we can skip the warnings for these unrealistic platforms.

The PNSE analyzer will not be added to the repo its just one time run  to detect missing annotations
